# Studios as First-Class Graph Citizens

> Child of **The Library Graph** (Epic, P0), which owns nodes, edges and D10 — *"a studio hierarchy is two nodes and a preference, not one name"*. This spec owns what the application does with that hierarchy: how it is **validated**, how it is **populated**, and how it is **shown**.
## Why this exists
Studios became `EntityProfile` rows in Phase C — correctly, per C1, because they genuinely have a logo, links and an external identity. But nothing in the application treats them as anything more than a string:
- The **profile page** is the actor page. A studio displays gender, hair colour, birth date and career span, and displays nothing about the one relationship that is genuinely its own.
- `studio_parent` had **0 rows** when this was written. D10's hierarchy exists in the schema and nowhere in the data.
- There is **no batch tool** for studios, though there is one for actors and one for videos — and studios are a node kind with an edge kind of their own.
## Findings from reading the code, 2026-08-06
Three constraints were discovered during design and changed it. Recorded because each was an assumption worth checking rather than believing.
**F1 — There is no ****`StudioMetadataProvider`****.** `Plugin.swift` defines `ActorMetadataProvider` and `VideoMetadataProvider` only, so studio facts arrive *only* as a by-product of matching a video. The source does already answer `searchStudio(term:limit:)` — used today by `studioId(named:)` in the plugin repo — but there is no fetch-by-id returning parent, aliases, urls or logo. A real Match Studios needs a new protocol **and** private-plugin-repo work.
**F2 — ****`AssetGridView`**** combines sidebar selections with ****`allSatisfy`****. It ANDs.** So showing a network's whole family by inserting each descendant as a `.studio(name)` item asks for videos belonging to *every* studio at once, which is zero for any real family. A family view needs its own `.studioFamily` case.
**F3 — Two conditions were detectable and surfaced nowhere.** A studio string with no `video_studio` edge behind it, and `LibraryStore.studioEdgeDisagreements()`, which already existed and nothing called.
## Decisions
| # | Decision | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Both tools, audit first.** Validate Studios needs no plugin work and establishes the true state before anything is built on it. Then Match Studios, then the profile page. | Decided 2026-08-06 |
| 2 | **The profile page comes last.** `studio_parent` is empty, so building it first produces a screen that is correct and blank for every studio in the library. | Decided 2026-08-06 |
| 3 | **The validator reports and routes; it never fixes.** Every repair already has a screen that does it carefully and asks the right question first. A validator that also repaired would be a second, less careful implementation of five existing tools. | Decided 2026-08-06 |
| 4 | **Family-wide video listing is deferred.** The lineage block ships without touching the grid — parent, siblings, children, each with a count, each a pivot. Per F2, a family filter needs a new `.studioFamily` case; that is the way in if it is picked up. | Decided 2026-08-06 |
| 5 | **A disagreeing parent is reported, never overwritten.** If a studio already carries a different parent, that is a genuine conflict about the world, and the graph's standing rule is that it refuses to guess. Follows GraphSync, which reports rather than resolves. | Decided 2026-08-06 |
| 6 | **Studio batch policy mirrors the actor one, decision for decision** — one candidate or it queues, fills only, logo never unattended, ambiguous skipped on re-runs. Three batch screens that behave differently is three things to learn. | Decided 2026-08-06 |
## Part 1 — Validate Studios
An audit in **Find Problems**, whose footer already promises *"These report rather than change anything."* Nine checks, sorted defects-first then by size, each naming the screen that resolves it.
| Check | Certain? | Routes to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Video carries two studios | defect | Fix Duplicate Studios |
| Two studios differ only by case or spacing | defect | Repair Tag Spelling |
| Studio string with no `video_studio` edge | defect | Connect the Graph |
| Edge disagrees with the tag | defect | Match Again |
| Network on record with no profile | defect | *none yet* |
| A studio inside itself | defect | *none yet* |
| Studio in use with no profile row | unfinished | Connect the Graph |
| Studio not confirmed against a source | unfinished | Match Studios |
| Studio profile no video uses | unfinished | Remove Orphaned Profiles |
Two implementation notes worth keeping:
- Spelling collisions fold through `StudioResolution.identity`, **not** `lowercased()`. The spellings that actually collide are the ones a source ran the spaces out of, so a case-only fold — what the tag audit does — misses the most common half.
- Two-studio videos are **excluded** from the missing-edge check. They have no edge *by design*, so counting them would report one defect twice and make the check impossible to clear while a conflict existed. `studioEdgeDisagreements()` excludes them for the same reason.
Single-library and disabled while federated, like Connect the Graph: half of what it checks is edges, and an edge cannot span two libraries.
## Part 2 — Match Studios
The direct analogue of Match Actors, and what actually populates `studio_parent` rather than waiting for every video to be re-matched.
Needs `StudioMetadataProvider` (`search(name:)` + `fetch(studioId:)` → a proposal carrying canonical name, aliases, parent name and id, urls, logo), plus the fetch-by-id in the private plugin repo. The parent fields have precedent: `VideoMetadataProposal` already carries `studioParent` and `studioParentSourceId`.
Two rules genuinely specific to studios, beyond the mirrored policy:
- **A studio match asserts a second node and an edge.** Confirming an imprint also asserts the network that owns it exists — one lookup yielding two profiles and a `studio_parent` row. This is the whole payoff. The parent is created via `confirmStudio`, already idempotent and non-destructive.
- **The run should report how much future asking it prevented.** `StudioResolution` falls to `.ask` when neither of two offered studios is verified. Every studio confirmed turns some number of those into `.use`, and that is the only tally that says what the run bought rather than what it did.
## Part 3 — The studio profile page
A studio branch in `ProfileGraphHeaderView`, parallel to the existing tag branch — not a new view. Tags already established that seam; a separate view would fork the photo browser, rename, delete and links four ways for one differing block.
- **Suppressed:** gender, hair colour, birth year, career span.
- **Kept:** logo (rounded rect, not a portrait circle), bio, home page and links, AKAs, rating.
- **Added:** the confirmation verdict as a badge — it is the input to `StudioResolution` and already the one fact `StudioGalleryView` surfaces.
- **Added:** the lineage block — parent, sibling imprints, children, each with a video count, each a pivot. Needs `childStudioIds(of:)` lifted out of `studioIdWithDescendants`, and a `videoIds(forStudio:)` that does not yet exist.
- **Changed:** "Co-Actors" reads **Actors** on a studio page. The "Studios" section is dropped — it lists studios *co-occurring on the same videos*, which is largely the two-studio defect; lineage replaces it with the real answer.
With `studio_parent` empty the block must degrade to one honest line — *"No network recorded yet. Match Studios can find it."* — rather than an empty box.

| `StudioLineage` — network, siblings, imprints, counts | Implemented | 10 tests; `LibraryStore.studioLineage(for:)`, `childStudioIds(of:)`, `parentStudioId(of:)`, `videoIds(forStudio:)`, `studioVideoCounts()` |
| Studio profile page — studio branch in `ProfileGraphHeaderView` | Implemented | person-only fields suppressed, verdict badge, lineage block, logo fit not fill; macOS + iOS build |

**Suite totals after all of the above:** LibraryCore 1,027 tests, 1 skipped, 0 failures. Plugin repo 129 tests, 4 skipped, 0 failures. macOS and iOS both build.
Two decisions taken while building Part 3, both about keeping the page honest:
- **Video counts come from the ****`studio:`**** TAGS, not from ****`video_studio`****.** The counts sit beside links that pivot the grid, and the grid filters on the string — counting edges would print a number the very next click contradicts. The edge is the better representation; until writes move to it, the display must agree with itself.
- **The header reloads on ****`ReloadAssets`****.** Match All Studios writes `studio_parent` and posts it. Without the subscription, a studio page open at the time keeps reading "no network recorded yet" after the run that recorded one — exactly what that message must never be wrong about.
D9 hygiene gate clean. All fixtures and examples use invented studio names — the gate cannot catch a real one.
⚠️ The plugin is symlinked file-by-file into the app target under `ViLM/LocalPlugins/ActorVideoMetadata/` (gitignored). A new plugin source file needs a symlink added there or the app cannot see it — the build fails with "cannot find X in scope" while the plugin package itself compiles cleanly.
## Outstanding operator work
63 videos across 31 groupings still carry two studios. These should be resolved through **Fix Duplicate Studios** before Match Studios runs: a video with two studios has no single studio to confirm, and *Connect the Graph* does not go back for what it skipped.
